fullPassage: In a place called Cottingley, England, in 1917, two young girls took some pictures of themselves near a stream at the bottom of a garden. The pictures showed the girls playing with fairies. When the famous author of Sherlock Holmes, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, found out about them, he wrote an article claiming that the pictures were proof of supernatural phenomena. In today's words, one could say that the pictures went "viral," and Doyle's endorsement gave the pictures "credibility." For several years, the girls maintained that the pictures were genuine. Only after almost seventy years did the girls finally admit that the whole thing was made up. While this story is an interesting anecdote of fake news involving a famous author, it may be a cautionary tale demonstrating the importance of media literacy in the digital age. In the past, knowledge was passed down directly by the spoken word. The credibility of the speaker, not what was said, was the measure of trustworthiness. When the printing press introduced books as a means of knowledge transfer and written materials became more prevalent, readers had to develop new critical evaluation skills. However, they were often limited to a single source to evaluate the writer's credibility, arguments, and logic. This type of analysis can be described as "vertical reading." Vertical reading involves relying on the text to determine the reliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author's credibility, their logic, and their references based on only their text. Having read a book, for example, a reader can review if the arguments presented in the text are supported by enough evidence, look at who the author or the publisher is, or check the references cited in the text. However, technology has changed the landscape in which people write and publish, making it necessary to change reading strategies. Since technology in 1917 was nowhere near as advanced as it is today, it's understandable that a few pictures could convince a famous author as well as the general public of the existence of fairies. Does advanced technology prevent people from being fooled now? In fact, it may make it even easier to get tricked. Many people today fall victim to hoaxes or accept false claims because they don't know how to verify information. This begs the question: How is it possible to verify such vast amounts of information? On the Internet, finding information is relatively easy, but verifying or validating it is not. In the past, there were publishing standards that authors had to meet. Today, the Internet removes the barriers to publishing for millions of people; however, it also makes it harder for readers to find reliable and valid information. In this environment, media literacy is more important than ever. Vertical reading is still useful, but new strategies must be adopted to navigate the vast online world. One of these strategies is called "lateral reading," which involves verifying information while reading by checking as many sources as you can. This is useful because only one source is not enough. Checking information from multiple sources with various types of content, such as text, images, and videos, is helpful to verify something you have read and gain insight. For example, suppose a student reads an article on a popular online news site about the health of a population of people. Having come across some statistics about the number of people who are hospitalized due to poor diet, she can employ the lateral reading strategy by simply opening up another tab in her browser and accessing different sources to verify the numbers. In fact, she can open up as many new tabs as she wants to verify any type of information being presented, such as statistics in charts and tables, or general assertions. She can look up information from other popular news sites or go directly to a scientific journal article to read from the primary source of information. Readers employing digital lateral reading can take advantage of the volume of information on the Internet to check the credibility of an author's claims. They can utilize Internet browser tools that help review many sites simultaneously. Many people and companies currently use this reading strategy because it allows them to more easily cross-check data, distinguish opinions from facts, and evaluate claims efficiently. As a way to maintain credibility, some companies hire "fact-checkers" to evaluate their writers' claims before publishing anything. These fact-checkers use lateral reading as a quick means to survey what has already been written. For example, imagine a news agency that wants to publish a story on its website about a merger between two corporations. Fact-checkers will cross-check information from a variety of sources to ensure that the facts are accurate. In fact, in recent research surveys, having utilized this strategy, participants were found to have a broader understanding of any kind of information than participants who had used less optimal strategies like vertical reading. Vertical reading is not a perfect strategy and neither is lateral reading, but lateral reading takes greater advantage of modern technology than vertical reading. To fully appreciate this strategy, a reader in the digital world makes evaluating all forms of information a habit. No matter how neutral an author or publication claims to be, the burden of evaluation falls upon the reader to survey as much information as possible to determine the credibility of the data or the claims. We need to understand that the world, and therefore information itself, is constantly evolving: information does not remain still, so neither should the reader. For this reason, lateral reading is a continuous, repetitive process. Instead of approaching media from the perspective of a mere consumer of information, readers must learn to actively and dynamically engage with it while trying to make sense of it.

❌ ② doubt(의심)은 '증거라고 주장했다'는 흐름과 반대
❌ ③ false(거짓의)는 '진짜라고 주장했다'는 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ absence(부재)는 '중요성을 보여준다'는 문맥과 반대
det.tip: proof=증거, genuine=진짜의, importance=중요성

det.tip: finding information is relatively easy(정보를 찾는 것은 비교적 쉽다) ↔ difficult(어려운)

questions.passage: Many people and companies currently use this reading strategy because it allows them to more easily cross-check data, distinguish opinions from facts, and evaluate claims efficiently. As a way to maintain credibility, some companies hire "fact-checkers" to evaluate their writers' claims before publishing anything. These fact-checkers use lateral reading as a quick means to survey what has already been written. For example, imagine a news agency that wants to publish a story on its website about a merger between two corporations. Fact-checkers will cross-check information from a variety of sources to ensure that the facts are accurate. In fact, in recent research surveys, having utilized this strategy, participants were found to have a <u>broader</u> understanding of any kind of information than participants who had used less optimal strategies like vertical reading.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 broader와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① wider: 더 넓은 (유의어라 반대 아님)
❌ ② deeper: 더 깊은 (의미축이 다름)
✅ ③ narrower: 더 좁은 ← 정답
❌ ④ longer: 더 긴 (의미축이 다름)
det.tip: a broader understanding(더 폭넓은 이해) ↔ narrower(더 좁은)

questions.passage:
(A) When you evaluate a claim, you should rely on the actual <u>text</u> itself, checking the author's logic and the evidence written in it before you decide whether the information is trustworthy.
(B) While I was on the bus, my friend sent me a short <u>text</u> on my phone to say that she would be about ten minutes late for our meeting.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 text의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① (A)는 '문자 메시지'가 아니라 '글·원문'임
❌ ② (A)는 '세금'이 아니라 '글·원문'임
❌ ③ (B)는 '글·원문'이 아니라 '문자 메시지'임
✅ ④ (A)의 text는 저자의 논리와 근거가 담긴 '글·원문'을 뜻하고(rely on the text itself), (B)의 text는 휴대폰으로 보낸 '문자 메시지'를 뜻함 ← 정답
det.tip: text: (A) 글·원문 / (B) 문자 메시지

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a false story or trick that is intended to make people believe something that is not true"

det.analysis:
❌ ① evidence(근거): 주장을 뒷받침하는 자료
✅ ② hoax(속임수): 사람들이 사실이 아닌 것을 믿게 하려는 거짓 이야기나 속임수 ← 정답
❌ ③ publisher(출판사): 책·글을 펴내는 곳
❌ ④ strategy(전략): 목표를 이루기 위한 계획
det.tip: fall victim to hoaxes = 속임수에 넘어가다 → hoax = 속임수

questions.passage: When the printing press introduced books as a means of knowledge transfer and written materials __________ (become) more prevalent, readers had to develop new critical evaluation skills. However, they were often limited to a single source to evaluate the writer's credibility, arguments, and logic.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: become(동사 원형) → became: 'When the printing press introduced ~ and written materials ___ more prevalent'에서 앞의 동사 introduced(과거)와 and로 이어지는 병렬 구조다. 과거 사실을 서술하므로 become을 과거시제 became으로 바꿔야 한다. '문서 자료가 더 보급되었을 때'라는 뜻이다.
det.tip: introduced와 병렬인 과거시제 → became

questions.passage: Having __________ (come) across some statistics about the number of people who are hospitalized due to poor diet, she can employ the lateral reading strategy by simply opening up another tab in her browser and accessing different sources to verify the numbers. In fact, she can open up as many new tabs as she wants to verify any type of information being presented, such as statistics in charts and tables, or general assertions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: come(동사 원형) → come: 문장 앞 'Having ___ across ~'는 'Having + 과거분사' 형태의 완료분사구문이다. 주절(she can employ ~)보다 먼저 일어난 일을 나타낸다. come은 불규칙 동사로 과거분사도 come이므로 Having come으로 써야 한다. '~을 접하고 나서'라는 뜻이다.
det.tip: Having + 과거분사(완료분사구문): Having come across(접하고 나서)

questions.passage: Vertical reading is still useful, but new strategies must be adopted to navigate the vast online world. One of these strategies is called "lateral reading," which involves verifying information while reading by checking as many sources as you can. This is useful because __________. Checking information from multiple sources with various types of content, such as text, images, and videos, is helpful to verify something you have read and gain insight. For example, suppose a student reads an article on a popular online news site about the health of a population of people. Having come across some statistics about the number of people who are hospitalized due to poor diet, she can employ the lateral reading strategy by simply opening up another tab in her browser and accessing different sources to verify the numbers. In fact, she can open up as many new tabs as she wants to verify any type of information being presented, such as statistics in charts and tables, or general assertions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 only one source is not enough(단일 출처만으로는 충분하지 않다)가 적절
det.analysis:
✅ ① only one source is not enough(단일 출처만으로는 충분하지 않다): 가로 읽기가 여러 출처를 확인하는 것이라고 설명한 뒤, 이것이 유용한 이유로 '단일 출처만으로는 충분하지 않기' 때문이라는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
❌ ② the Internet is always correct(인터넷은 항상 옳다): 본문은 정보 검증의 필요성을 강조하므로 반대
❌ ③ reading quickly saves time(빨리 읽으면 시간을 아낀다): 본문에 없는 내용
❌ ④ books are better than websites(책이 웹사이트보다 낫다): 매체 우열 비교가 아님
det.tip: checking as many sources as you can ~ because only one source is not enough: 단일 출처로는 부족하기 때문

ch: only one source is not enough

questions.passage: Vertical reading is not a perfect strategy and neither is lateral reading, but lateral reading takes greater advantage of modern technology than vertical reading. To fully appreciate this strategy, a reader in the digital world makes evaluating all forms of information a habit. No matter how neutral an author or publication claims to be, the burden of evaluation falls upon the reader to survey as much information as possible to determine the credibility of the data or the claims. We need to understand that the world, and therefore information itself, is constantly evolving: information does not remain still, so neither should the reader. For this reason, lateral reading is a continuous, repetitive process. Instead of approaching media from the perspective of a mere consumer of information, readers must learn to __________ while trying to make sense of it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 actively and dynamically engage with it(능동적이고 역동적으로 그것을 다루다)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① passively accept whatever they read(읽는 것을 수동적으로 받아들이다): '단순 소비자의 관점 대신'이라는 대비 흐름과 반대
❌ ② avoid reading online news entirely(온라인 뉴스를 전혀 읽지 않다): 본문 취지(능동적 평가)와 무관
✅ ③ actively and dynamically engage with it(능동적이고 역동적으로 그것을 다루다): 단순한 정보 소비자가 아니라 정보를 이해하려 애쓰며 '능동적이고 역동적으로 다루는' 법을 배워야 한다는 문맥에 적절 ← 정답
❌ ④ memorize every detail of the text(원문의 모든 세부를 암기하다): 암기가 아니라 능동적 평가가 핵심
det.tip: Instead of ~ a mere consumer, readers must learn to actively and dynamically engage with it: 능동적·역동적으로 다루다

ch: actively and dynamically engage with it
memorize every detail of the text
